Invisalign vs. Metal Braces: A Cost and Comfort Comparison

Dr. Viddulata Jagtap

Senior Dentist

January 25, 2025

Is it too late to straighten my teeth?

We hear this question almost every day at Shriyan Dental Clinic. Many adults in Pune assume that if they didn't get braces as a teenager, they missed their window. They want straight teeth, but they can't imagine walking into a board meeting or a wedding with metal brackets glued to their teeth.

The good news? Orthodontics has changed. You no longer have to choose between a straight smile and your professional appearance.


Enter Invisalign. But is it actually better than traditional Metal Braces? And is the price difference worth it?

Let’s break down the battle of the braces.


The Contender: Traditional Metal Braces

These are the braces you remember from high school—stainless steel brackets glued to the teeth, connected by a wire.

  • The Pros: Incredibly effective at fixing severe overcrowding and complex bite issues. Since they are fixed, they work 24/7 (great for teens who might forget trays).
  • The Cons: Highly visible, diet restrictions (no popcorn/sticky candy), and flossing can be difficult. Wires can sometimes poke.

The Challenger: Invisalign (Invisalign®)

Invisalign uses a series of custom-made, transparent plastic trays that gently push your teeth into the correct position.

  • Invisible: Virtually undetectable. Perfect for working professionals in places like Magarpatta City or college students who want to look their best.
  • Removable: Take them out to eat, meaning zero food restrictions.
  • Comfort: Smooth plastic means no ulcers on your cheeks.
  • Hygiene: Brush and floss normally.

The Catch: You must have the discipline to wear them for 20–22 hours a day.


The Comparison: Cost and Timeline

1. How long does it take?

  • Braces: Typically 18 to 24 months.
  • Invisalign: Typically 12 to 18 months (often faster due to targeted force).

2. What about the Cost?

Historically, clear aligners were significantly more expensive. However, the gap has closed. While aligners generally have a higher upfront cost due to lab fees, many patients find the lifestyle benefits worth every rupee.


The Verdict: Which Should You Choose?

Choose Metal Braces If: You have complex bite issues, are on a strict budget, or might lose removable trays.

Choose Invisalign If: Aesthetics are your priority, you want to eat freely, and you are disciplined enough to wear them.
